**8B.6 Research Note: Sheikh Hasina in 2024**
Claim-level evidence on whether declarations became observable implementation and state reach, rather than remaining slogans.

**Supports implementation**
- **BSS | January 11, 2024 | https://b.bssnews.net/news-flash/167551**  
  Hasina formed a 37-member cabinet that included two technocrats, which is limited but real evidence of putting some capable specialists into executive roles rather than relying only on slogans or pure party theater.  
  IDs: `8B.6`, `8B.4`

- **Dhaka Tribune | April 16, 2024 | https://www.dhakatribune.com/amp/bangladesh/344095/official-document-govt-to-include-smart**  
  The planning commission sought to embed “Smart Bangladesh” into the Ninth Five Year Plan with targets for macro stability, inflation control, jobs, poverty reduction, regional balance, and rule of law. This is one of the clearest signs that a campaign slogan was being translated into formal state planning.  
  IDs: `8B.6`, `8B.1`, `8B.3`

- **Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority | March 6, 2024 | https://bppa.gov.bd/media-communication/news-1446.html**  
  BPPA said e-GP was mandatory for government agencies, with broad registration and improved transparency, efficiency, and competition. That is concrete administrative implementation, not just declaratory rhetoric.  
  IDs: `8B.6`, `8B.3`, `8B.4`

- **UNB | June 4, 2024 | https://unb.com.bd/category/Bangladesh/govt-adopts-plan-to-turn-public-welfare-services-into-smart-services-in-two-years/136812**  
  The government moved 52 ministries and divisions into a Smart Bangladesh implementation platform for “smart” welfare services. This is strong whole-of-government rollout evidence.  
  IDs: `8B.6`, `8B.1`, `8B.3`

- **WHO Bangladesh | March 4, 2024 | https://www.who.int/bangladesh/news/detail/04-03-2024-advancing-healthcare-excellence-who-s-role-in-developing-the-first-national-medical-education-strategy-in-bangladesh**  
  The health ministry, with WHO support, launched Bangladesh’s first national medical education strategy using workforce studies and a technical working group. This is concrete evidence of policy turning into bureaucratic action.  
  IDs: `8B.6`, `8B.3`

- **WHO | July 11, 2024 | https://www.who.int/southeastasia/news/detail/11-07-2024-2nd-jee-bn**  
  Bangladesh completed a peer-reviewed Joint External Evaluation that identified strengths, gaps, and priority actions. This shows a functioning measurement-and-correction mechanism inside the state apparatus.  
  IDs: `8B.6`, `8B.3`, `8B.4`

- **World Bank | June 21, 2024 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/21/bangladesh-receives-900-million-world-bank-financing-to-increase-economic-and-urban-resilience-for-sustainable-growth**  
  The Bank described reforms covering fiscal policy, banking oversight, procurement reform, and resilience spending. This is real institutional follow-through, though still reform-design level rather than proof of durable success.  
  IDs: `8B.6`, `8B.3`

- **WHO Bangladesh | June 22, 2024 | https://www.who.int/bangladesh/news/detail/22-06-2024-who-bangladesh-celebrates-landmark-success-of-the-health-and-gender-support-project-in-cox-s-bazar**  
  The project, run through the Ministry of Health and World Bank funding, produced quantified outputs like screenings, trained workers, and expanded surveillance capacity. This is direct evidence of implementation reaching a vulnerable area.  
  IDs: `8B.6`, `8B.3`, `8B.5`

- **World Bank | May 28, 2024 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/05/28/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-provide-basic-services-opportunities-and-build-resilience-for-displaced-rohingya-and-host-co**  
  World Bank-backed projects funded health, nutrition, education, water, shelters, livelihoods, and GBV prevention for Rohingya and host communities. This shows targeted policy execution beyond rhetoric, though it was heavily partner-financed.  
  IDs: `8B.6`, `8B.5`, `8B.8`

- **World Bank | June 28, 2024 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/28/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-develop-bay-terminal**  
  The Bay Terminal project was framed as a trade-competitiveness investment to reduce import/export costs and improve port efficiency. This is another example of declaration being carried into concrete infrastructure planning.  
  IDs: `8B.6`, `8B.3`

**Cuts against implementation**
- **Reuters | January 4, 2024 | https://theprint.in/world/little-election-fizz-in-bangladesh-as-prime-minister-set-for-another-term/1910693/**  
  Reuters reported the opposition boycott followed Hasina’s refusal to resign and allow a neutral authority to run the election. This indicates that some public democratic language was not matched by institutionally neutral implementation.  
  IDs: `8B.6`, `8B.1`, `8B.4`

- **Reuters | July 20, 2024 | https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/**  
  The government answered unrest with curfew, troop deployment, roadblocks, and internet/text shutdowns. That is implementation, but of coercive control and information suppression rather than public-program delivery.  
  IDs: `8B.6`, `8B.5`, `8B.8`

- **Reuters | July 22, 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153**  
  Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed political opponents for the violence. This reads as regime defense and blame-shifting, not transparent follow-through on a constructive governing agenda.  
  IDs: `8B.6`, `8B.5`, `8B.8`

- **UN OHCHR | July 26, 2024 | https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights**  
  The UN said more than 170 people were killed and warned that internet shutdowns increased impunity. This is strong evidence that state reach existed, but in a coercive form that undercut any claim of constructive implementation.  
  IDs: `8B.6`, `8B.5`, `8B.8`

- **The Daily Star | April 20, 2024 | https://www.thedailystar.net/opinion/views/news/bangladeshs-nuclear-prestige-illusion-3590666**  
  This opinion piece argued the Rooppur second-plant push looked prestige-driven amid debt and inflation. It is not decisive proof, but it is credible evidence that some headline projects risked staying symbolic or image-driven.  
  IDs: `8B.6`, `8B.4`

- **TBS News | October 5, 2024 | https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/energy/rooppur-power-plant-was-al-govts-white-elephant-energy-sector-experts-958801**  
  Energy-sector experts described Rooppur as a white-elephant project tied to mismanagement and corruption. This is negative evidence that not all flagship declarations translated into clean, effective implementation.  
  IDs: `8B.6`, `8B.4`, `8B.5`

**Assessment**
- Best-supported positive finding: Hasina’s government did convert some 2024 declarations into visible implementation, especially in procurement digitization, Smart Bangladesh planning, health-sector technical work, and selected infrastructure/humanitarian tracks.
- Best-supported negative finding: implementation quality was uneven and in the July crisis the state’s reach was coercive, opaque, and rights-abusive rather than programmatic.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a single independent 2024 whole-of-government scorecard showing how fully “Smart Bangladesh” or other major promises were implemented across ministries, districts, and agencies. The evidence is mostly sectoral, process-level, or partner-driven, so broad conclusions about overall state reach remain partly inferential rather than directly measured.
